feeds.title: Chris Naunton Blog
feeds.description: Explore the blog for articles on the history of ancient Egypt, author's travels and more! Dr Chris Naunton is an Egyptologist, writer and broadcaster.

feeds.title: Ancient Egypt Alive Blog
feeds.description: Explore the fascinating glories and the mystical stories of Ancient Egyptians with us! Ancient Egypt Alive! is a Canadian organization devoted to raising interest, knowledge and excitement around the study and preservation of ancient Egypt.

feeds.title: Hannah Pethen
feeds.description: Find articles on Archaeology and Egyptology in the 21st century. Current archaeological fieldwork, survey, technology and opinion, with a particular focus on Egypt. Freelance archaeologist and independent researcher, specialising in satellite remote sensing, GIS, archaeological survey and the archaeology of ancient Egypt.

feeds.title: Egypt at the Manchester Museum
feeds.description: Everything Egyptian at the Manchester Museum.The Manchester Museum houses over 18,000 objects from ancient Egypt and Sudan, making one of the largest collections in Britain and one with world-class holdings in a number of areas.

feeds.title: Tales from the Two Lands
feeds.description: Find Snippets from the fascinating history & culture of Ancient Egypt. Tales from the Two Lands grew out of a desire to share the cool things I learn about Ancient Egypt with other people. My name is Margaret Lucy Patterson, and I write the words and take most of the photos for this website.

feeds.title: Ancient Egypt Blog
feeds.description: Learn ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs and dive into the rich history of ancient Egypt with the Ancient Egypt Blog. Author Nicole is a self-taught Egyptologist and shares her passion for amazing Ancient history Books, Blogs, Videos, Explaining artifacts, and much more.

feeds.title: Tim The Egyptians Blog
feeds.description: Explore the history of Egypt, the culture of ancient Egypt and more!

feeds.title: Nile Scribes
feeds.description: Moderated by Toronto-based Taylor and Thomas, Nile Scribes is a dual-language blog with weekly posts on the latest in Egyptology. Our blog aims to keep you engaged with what is happening in the field by sharing Interviews with Egyptologists, Introductions to the latest publications, Summaries of Egyptological lectures and events in our area and Reviews of how Egypt is adapted for entertainment like films and theatre.

feeds.title: Nicky Van De Beek
feeds.description: Explore the ancient history of egypt, excavation articles, research and more! Nicky van de Beek MA studied Egyptology, Archaeology and Digital Humanities at Leiden University in the Netherlands.

feeds.title: Ancient Egypt Daily
feeds.description: A blog dedicated to the history and art of Ancient Egypt.

feeds.title: The Media Line » Egyptology
feeds.description: Explore the latest in Egyptology, news on new findings, excavations and more! An independent American news agency specializing in coverage of the Middle East. The Media Line provides unbiased reporting, background and context.

feeds.title: Egypt Centre Collection Blog
feeds.description: This is a regular blog dealing with the Egypt Centre collection of Swansea. Ken Griffin Collections Access Manager at the Egypt Centre.

feeds.title: The Curious Egyptologist Blog
feeds.description: Dive into weekly articles exploring the History, Culture, and Common life in Ancient Egypt. Each new post is filled with a new informative topic and discussion that the author found fascinating. The author is a budding Egyptologist who likes to share her curiosity on the web.

feeds.title: The Ancient Egypt Heritage and Archeology Fund Blog
feeds.description: The Ancient Egyptian Heritage and Archaeology Fund is a registered 501c3, private, nonprofit organization with a mission is to support research and conservation on Egyptian history and culture. In particular, it seeks to record and publish sites and monuments at risk from agricultural and urban expansion, looting, and vandalism.

feeds.title: Hair And Death In Ancient Egypt
feeds.description: Mourners, priests, mummies, gods... All of them took part in the funerary ceremony of ancient Egypt, all of them contributed to the dead's resurrection and all of them had a role in every rite. Ancient Egypt documents showing what happened in the Egyptian funerary ceremony. Mª Rosa Valdesogo Martín (Madrid, 1968), is graduate in Ancient History and Archaeology in University of Barcelona (UB) (Spain). While she was in the University she worked in archaeological sites in Spain and France (Paleolithic and Roman) digging and classifying materials.

feeds.title: The Eloquent Peasant
feeds.description: An Egyptology blog in which I write about a range of ancient Egyptian issues, including current news, my own work, and Egyptian life and culture. My name is Margaret Maitland and I am currently Principal Curator of the Ancient Mediterranean at National Museums Scotland in Edinburgh, where I am also Head of the Mediterranean, Africa, Americas, and Oceania section in the Department of World Cultures.

feeds.title: Ancient Egypt Magazine
feeds.description: Ancient Egypt is the world's leading Egyptology magazine, exploring the history, people and culture of the Nile Valley. Now in a larger format with a fresh new design, AE brings you the latest news and discoveries, and feature articles covering more than 5000 years of Egyptian history.

feeds.title: Egypt Museum
feeds.description: Egypt Museum is a virtual collection of ancient Egyptian art, culture and history. Sharing the treasures in museums and exhibitions from across the world in one place. Enjoy browsing the endless artifacts and jewelry, artworks and sculptures, tombs, temple reliefs, and even mummies that will be shared with you here.
